title: Moab Travel Guide

hero.headline: Moab Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Plan a high-value Moab itinerary with top neighborhoods, outdoor access, and proven tour ideas.

overview: Moab sits between Arches National Park and Canyonlands National Park, with red-rock mesas, river corridors, and a compact downtown.
The city is a base for hiking, scenic drives, and off-road routes across the Colorado Plateau.

highlights.title: Signature sights in Moab
highlights.description: Start with landmark districts and viewpoints during early hours.

highlights.title: Local neighborhoods
highlights.description: Balance top attractions with one neighborhood known for food and culture.

highlights.title: Outdoor access
highlights.description: Use guided trips for nearby parks, water routes, or scenic drives.

highlights.title: Evening experiences
highlights.description: Reserve one night for live entertainment, dining, or waterfront walks.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Arches National Park
thingsToDo.description: Arches National Park contains more than 2,000 natural sandstone arches just north of Moab. Delicate Arch, Balanced Rock, and Devils Garden define the park's high-desert landscape.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Canyonlands National Park
thingsToDo.description: Canyonlands National Park protects deep canyons carved by the Colorado and Green rivers. The Island in the Sky district near Moab provides broad overlooks above layered desert basins.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Dead Horse Point State Park
thingsToDo.description: Dead Horse Point State Park sits on a high mesa above a major Colorado River bend. The park is known for cliff-edge viewpoints and short rim trails west of Moab.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Colorado River
thingsToDo.description: The Colorado River runs directly past Moab and shapes the city's canyon geography. Rafting sections, river beaches, and viewpoints along Highway 128 anchor many outdoor itineraries.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Hell’s Revenge
thingsToDo.description: Hell’s Revenge is a slickrock trail system east of Moab used for 4x4 and UTV routes. Steep sandstone fins and open desert views make it one of the area's signature motorized terrain zones.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Downtown Moab
thingsToDo.description: Downtown Moab is the service and commercial core for regional park travel. Main Street concentrates gear shops, tour operators, restaurants, and local museums in a compact corridor.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Corona Arch
thingsToDo.description: Corona Arch is a large freestanding sandstone arch west of Moab near the Colorado River corridor. A moderate out-and-back trail reaches the arch through open slickrock and railroad canyon terrain.

thingsToDo.title: Explore La Sal Mountains
thingsToDo.description: The La Sal Mountains rise southeast of Moab as a high-elevation range above the desert basin. Alpine forests, cooler temperatures, and mountain viewpoints contrast sharply with nearby canyon country.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Shoulder seasons are best for comfort and flexibility
bullets: Spring and fall typically offer the easiest weather for walking and tours.
Summer can be busy; reserve major attractions and timed entries early.
Winter trips can provide better rates and lighter midday crowds in many districts.

travelTips: Group park visits by region to avoid repeated highway loops.
Book timed-entry or permit-based activities before peak dates.
Carry extra water, sun protection, and a backup indoor stop for heat or storms.

faq.q: How many days are ideal for Moab?
faq.a: Three to four days gives enough time for major attractions and one outdoor-focused day.

faq.q: Is Moab strong for outdoor recreation?
faq.a: Yes. Most itineraries can combine city highlights with nearby hiking, water, or scenic touring options.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: Yes—book ahead for weekends, holidays, and peak seasons.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Moab is a gateway city for southeastern Utah parks, canyons, and desert trail systems.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: Moab lies along the Colorado River below sandstone cliffs and high-desert mesas near the La Sal Mountains.

sections.heading: History (brief)
paragraphs: Moab developed as a river crossing, agricultural settlement, and later an access point for mining and national-park travel.

sections.heading: Culture & neighborhoods
paragraphs: Downtown Moab centers on Main Street with outfitters, local restaurants, galleries, and park services.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Spring and fall bring the strongest hiking and biking conditions; summer heat shifts activity to early and late daylight hours.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Most major trailheads and park roads require driving from town; downtown itself is walkable.
